evidence.description: String 'Nozzle Voltage' found in firmware, indicating UI/monitoring for nozzle voltage control
Hardware: 6x CM504B hex level shifters provide direct GPIO to HP45 nozzles. No shift registers, direct pin control. 128-pin N32903K5DN has ample GPIO.
N3290x Timer Controller specification (pages 669-672). TMR_BA @ 0xB8002000 not referenced in firmware.

next_steps: Search firmware for GPIO configuration code (GPA/GPC/GPD/GPE/GPB setup)
Verify HP04 source pin (currently TBD in finding-0016)
Trace C10X/CTSR sensor pins to ADC inputs
Identify delay routine for ~1.8µs pulse timing
provenance: Hardware PCB reverse engineering + firmware string analysis, 2025-11-27 to 2025-12-01
raw_note:
Complete HP45 Control Architecture:

Cartridge Matrix (see finding-0014):
- 300 nozzles in 22×14 matrix
- 22 address lines (HA0-HA21) select row
- 14 primitive lines (HP0-HP13) fire nozzles in selected row
- Operating voltage: VDD ~12V, pulse duration ~1.8µs

Address Lines HA0-HA21 (see finding-0015):
  IC3 (CM504B): HA00-HA05 ← GPC0-GPC5   (SoC pins 49-44)
  IC4 (CM504B): HA06-HA11 ← GPC6-GPC11  (SoC pins 43-38)
  IC5 (CM504B): HA12-HA17 ← GPC12-15, GPE0-1 (SoC pins 37-32)
  IC6 (CM504B): HA18-HA21 ← GPB15, GPD9-11 (SoC pins 54,52-50)

Primitive Lines HP0-HP13 (see finding-0016):
  Via IC1 (CM504B) + Q7-Q9 (MOSFETs):
    HP00 ← GPA0 (pin 79), HP01 ← GPA1 (pin 78)
    HP02 ← GPA4 (pin 75), HP03 ← GPA2 (pin 77)
    HP04 ← [TBD],         HP05 ← GPA5 (pin 74)
  
  Via IC2 (CM504B) + Q10-Q12 (MOSFETs):
    HP06 ← GPA6 (pin 73),  HP07 ← GPA7 (pin 103)
    HP08 ← GPD5 (pin 113), HP09 ← GPA10/11 (pin 122/123)
    HP10 ← GPA7 (pin 103), HP11 ← GPD6 (pin 112)
  
  Via IC6 (CM504B) + Q13 (MOSFETs):
    HP12 ← GPD7 (pin 115), HP13 ← GPD8 (pin 114)

Hardware Components (see finding-0017):
- 6× CM504B hex level shifters (3.3V → 12V)
- 7× Dual N-MOSFET packages (Q7-Q13, marking 'DS01', SOT-23-6)
- High-side switching topology for HP primitives

Expected Firmware Pattern:
for address in 0..21:  # 22 address phases
    set_HA(address)              # One bit in GPC/GPE/GPB/GPD
    hp_mask = bitmap[address]    # 14-bit mask for GPA/GPD
    set_HP_mask(hp_mask)         # High-side MOSFETs on
    delay_us(1.8)                # Heating pulse
    clear_HP_mask()
    clear_HA(address)

UI Strings Found:
- 'Nozzle Voltage' @ VA 0x001f2cf4
- 'Cartridge Type' @ VA 0x001f2df8  
- 'Cartridge Num.' @ VA 0x001f2ba8
- Error messages for cartridge abnormalities

Timing:
- No TMR_BA (0xB8002000) references found → likely busy-wait delays
- Pulse duration critical: ~1.5-2.0µs per HP45 spec

Sensor Pins (C10X/CTSR):
- 10X: Reference resistor (~300Ω)
- TSR: Temperature sensor (~300Ω, 11Ω per 10°C)
- Purpose: Voltage monitoring, temperature-based pulse adjustment
- Status: Not yet traced to ADC pins on PCB
summary: Complete hardware reverse engineering of HP45 cartridge control. The printer uses 6× CM504B level shifters and 7× dual N-MOSFETs to drive the HP45's 22×14 nozzle matrix. Pin mapping identified: HA0-HA21 address lines on GPC0-15/GPE0-1/GPB15/GPD9-11, HP0-HP13 primitive lines on GPA0-11/GPD5-8. Firmware should implement 22-phase loop with ~1.8µs pulse timing per nozzle. UI strings confirm nozzle voltage monitoring. See findings 0014-0017 for detailed specifications.
title: HP45 Cartridge Control - Complete Pin Mapping and Driver Architecture
